original_value: With the widespread development of location-based services, the demand for accurate indoor positioning is getting more and more urgent. Floor positioning, as a prerequisite for indoor positioning in multi-story buildings, is particularly important. Though lots of work has been done on floor positioning, the existing studies on floor positioning in complex multi-story buildings with large hollow areas through multiple floors still cannot meet the application requirements because of low accuracy and robustness. To obtain accurate and robust floor estimation in complex multi-story buildings, we propose a novel floor positioning method, which combines the Wi-Fi based floor positioning (BWFP), the barometric pressure-based floor positioning (BPFP) with HMM and the XGBoost based user motion detection. Extensive experiments show that using our proposed method can achieve 99.2% accuracy, which outperforms other state-of-the-art floor estimation methods.

result.paraphrase: As location-based services have spread widely, the need for accurate indoor positioning has become increasingly urgent. In multi-story buildings, floor positioning is a prerequisite for indoor localization and is especially critical. Although much research has been devoted to floor positioning, current methods for complex multi-story buildings with large hollow spaces spanning multiple floors still fall short of practical requirements due to insufficient accuracy and robustness. To achieve reliable and precise floor estimation in such environments, we propose a new floor positioning approach that integrates Wi-Fi-based floor positioning (BWFP), barometric pressure-based floor positioning (BPFP) with HMM, and XGBoost-based user motion detection. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method reaches 99.2% accuracy, surpassing other state-of-the-art floor estimation techniques.
